requirements.requirement: node1 has a routed interface inside each VLAN (facing node2's subnet and node3's subnet) with IPs assigned
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 assigned 192.168.11.1/24 (node2's VLAN) and eth2 assigned 192.168.12.1/24 (node3's VLAN), confirmed via direct ip addr output. Config also persisted to /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-vlan-routing and survived node1's later restart with the same addresses re-observed.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards traffic between the two VLANs (IP forwarding enabled on the routed interfaces)
requirements.summary: net.ipv4.ip_forward, conf.all.forwarding, conf.eth1.forwarding, and conf.eth2.forwarding all set to 1 on node1, persisted to /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf, and re-confirmed intact after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 (each on their own subnet/VLAN behind node1) can reach each other across the VLAN boundary
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ping between node2 (192.168.11.2) and node3 (192.168.12.2) succeeds with TTL=63 (one hop lower than a direct TTL=64, consistent with routing through node1), both before and after all three nodes were restarted. Static routes via node1 were configured on both node2 and node3.

overall_summary: The core contract is satisfied: node1 (SONiC) has routed interfaces with correct addressing inside both node2's and node3's VLANs, IP forwarding is enabled on node1, and node2/node3 demonstrably reach each other across the VLAN boundary via node1 (TTL=63 confirms the routed hop). The executor also ran the mandatory provider-wide restart protocol on all three nodes: for each node the evidence shows a pre-restart baseline boot_id, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered interface/route/forwarding state plus a re-verified cross-VLAN ping, and these boot_id transitions are cross-confirmed by the fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots. Configuration was also persisted to disk (SONiC interfaces.d + sysctl.d; Alpine /etc/network/interfaces with route hooks), which is not itself demanded by the public task wording but strengthens confidence that the solution is durable, not a one-off manual state.
limitations: Persistence/reboot-survival of the routing configuration is not explicitly required by the public task wording; it was demonstrated anyway via the independent restart protocol, but is treated here as supporting evidence rather than a scored requirement.

node1's after-executor snapshot shows 'system-health.service' newly listed as failed compared to before-prepare; no executor command clearly targets or explains this service, so it is noted as an unexplained but likely reboot-related artifact rather than attributed to a specific mutation.

The reboot acknowledgement commands for node2 and node3 show the exec stream closing before completion (return_code -1, 'exec stream closed before command completion'), which is expected for a command that triggers its own connection drop, but means the ack itself wasn't a clean return_code 0 confirmation; the subsequent boot_id change is the stronger evidence of an actual restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to task prerequisites (interface IP assignment, forwarding sysctls, static routes, persistence files) or to the independently-required restart protocol. One tangential mutation on node1 (cmd-3ec589cdb2a9481b) removed docker0's pre-existing 240.127.1.1/24 address and brought docker0 down as part of the same command that assigned eth1/eth2 addresses; this wasn't clearly necessary to configure the routed interfaces and had no stated rationale in the report. It was low-risk and self-reverted: after node1's later restart, docker0 came back up with its original 240.127.1.1/24 address (cmd-436dfbfa0f204383), so no residue remained. A separate exploratory attempt to use SONiC's native `config interface ip add` CLI (cmd-8484cab85f174723) failed with a usage error and caused no state change before the executor fell back to direct `ip addr add` — this is a harmless failed attempt, not a mutation. After the final restart, node1's failed-services list gained 'system-health.service' (SONiC's health monitor) that wasn't failed at before-prepare; this looks like an artifact of the reboot cycle on this SONiC image rather than a result of any specific executor mutation, and is noted as a limitation rather than a hygiene fault.
